ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, let P be any point on side BC of the equilateral $\triangle ABC$. Point D lies on the extension of side BA. Rotate line segment PD $60^\circ$ counterclockwise around point P to obtain line segment PE. Connect BE. What is the measure of $\angle CBE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $DF \parallel AC$ passing through point $D$ and intersecting the extension of $BC$ at point $F$, as shown in the figure: \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC = \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAC = \angle BDF = \angle BCA = \angle F = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DBF$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DB = DF$,\\
$\because$ rotating segment $PD$ $60^\circ$ counterclockwise around point $P$ results in segment $PE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle PDE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DE = DP$, $\angle EDP = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDB + \angle BDP = \angle PDF + \angle BDP = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDB = \angle PDF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EDB \cong \triangle PDF$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EBD = \angle F = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBE = \angle ABC + \angle EBD = \boxed{120^\circ}$

First read the diagram as an equilateral triangle ABC with A above the horizontal base BC and P located on segment BC; D and E are defined by the text rather than visibly shown in the attached partial figure. Use the text to place D on the extension ray of BA beyond A, rotate PD counterclockwise by 60 degrees about P to get PE, and connect BE. Construct a new point F by drawing through D a line parallel to AC, meeting the extension of BC at F. Because ABC is equilateral, the angles made by DB, DF, and BF are all 60 degrees, so triangle DBF is equilateral and DB = DF. The rotation condition makes triangle PDE equilateral, so DE = DP and angle EDP = 60 degrees. Compare the angles at D: angle EDB equals angle PDF because both are obtained by subtracting angle BDP from a 60-degree angle. Since BD is the same ray as BA and angle ABC = 60 degrees, angle CBE = 60 degrees + 60 degrees = 120 degrees.

先描述图像：图中底边 BC 是水平线段，B 在左、C 在右，A 在上方，三角形 ABC 呈等边三角形形状；点 P 位于边 BC 上，靠近 C。图中未画出 D、E，但题文给出 D 在 BA 的延长线上，PD 绕 P 逆时针旋转 60° 得到 PE。
再推理：按指定坐标法，设 B=(0,0)，C=(1,0)，A=(1/2,√3/2)，于是射线 BA 与正 x 轴方向 BC 成 60°。令 P=(p,0)，0≤p≤1。因为 D 在 BA 过 A 的延长线上，可写为 D=(t/2,√3t/2)，t>1。由旋转定义，E=P+R60(D-P)，其中 R60(x,y)=(x/2-√3y/2,√3x/2+y/2)。
计算 D-P=(t/2-p,√3t/2)。旋转后得到 R60(D-P)=(-(t+p)/2,√3(t-p)/2)，所以 E=(p,0)+R60(D-P)=((p-t)/2,√3(t-p)/2)。
因此向量 BE=E-B=((p-t)/2,√3(t-p)/2)=(t-p)/2·(-1,√3)。由于 t>1 且 p≤1，比例系数为正，所以 BE 的方向就是向量 (-1,√3) 的方向。它相对于正 x 轴，即射线 BC 的方向，夹角为 120°。所以 ∠CBE=120°。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, let P be any point on side BC of the equilateral $\triangle ABC$. Point D lies on the extension of side BA. Rotate line segment PD $60^\circ$ counterclockwise around point P to obtain line segment PE. Connect BE. What is the measure of $\angle CBE$ in degrees?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $DF \parallel AC$ passing through point $D$ and intersecting the extension of $BC$ at point $F$, as shown in the figure: \\
$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC = \angle BAC = \angle BCA = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle BAC = \angle BDF = \angle BCA = \angle F = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle DBF$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DB = DF$,\\
$\because$ rotating segment $PD$ $60^\circ$ counterclockwise around point $P$ results in segment $PE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle PDE$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $DE = DP$, $\angle EDP = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDB + \angle BDP = \angle PDF + \angle BDP = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDB = \angle PDF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EDB \cong \triangle PDF$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EBD = \angle F = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CBE = \angle ABC + \angle EBD = \boxed{120^\circ}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The attached figure shows a triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right; BC is the horizontal base. Point P is marked on side BC and is near C. D, E, or the auxiliary point F are not directly drawn in the figure; they are determined by the problem text and the construction.
Reasoning: According to the problem, △ABC is an equilateral triangle, so ∠ABC=∠BAC=∠BCA=60°. Point D is on the extension of BA, therefore B, A, D are collinear. Through D draw DF∥AC, intersecting the extension of BC at F. Since DF∥AC, and DB is collinear with BA, BF is collinear with BC, it can be obtained that ∠BDF=∠BAC=60°, ∠DFB=∠ACB=60°, so △DBF is an equilateral triangle, hence DB=DF.
Also because line segment PD is rotated counterclockwise by 60° around point P to obtain PE, so PD=PE and ∠DPE=60°, thus △PDE is an equilateral triangle, hence DE=DP, and ∠EDP=60°.
At point D, ∠EDB+∠BDP=∠EDP=60°; at the same time, because △DBF is equilateral and P is on the line where BF lies, ∠PDF+∠BDP=∠BDF=60°. Therefore ∠EDB=∠PDF.
Thus △EDB and △PDF satisfy DE=DP, DB=DF, and the included angles ∠EDB=∠PDF, so △EDB≅△PDF. Corresponding angles are equal, obtaining ∠EBD=∠DFP=60°.
Since BD and BA are in the same ray direction, ∠ABC=60°, so ∠CBE=∠ABC+∠EBD=60°+60°=120°.
